sanskrit: pravṛddhadhvajamaṇḍūkāṃ bherīvistīrṇakacchapām chatrahaṃsāvalījuṣṭāṃ phenacāmaramālinīm
english: Its frogs were the upreared standards, its broad turtles the kettledrums; it was thronged with rows of swans that were the parasols, and garlanded with foam that was the yak-tail whisks.

sanskrit: kaṅkagṛdhramahāgrāhāṃ naikāyudhajhaṣākulām rathakṣiptamahāvaprāṃ patākāruciradrumām
english: Its great crocodiles were herons and vultures, and it teemed with fish that were the manifold weapons; chariots flung up were its high banks, and its lovely trees were the bright pennons.

sanskrit: śaramīnāṃ mahāraudrāṃ prāsaśaktyugraḍuṇḍubhām majjāmāṃsamahāpaṅkāṃ kabandhāvarjitoḍupām
english: Most terrible it was, with arrows for its small fish and lances and spears for its fierce water-snakes; marrow and flesh were its deep mire, and headless trunks the boats adrift upon it.

sanskrit: keśaśaivalakalmāṣāṃ bhīrūṇāṃ kaśmalāvahām nāgendrahayayodhānāṃ śarīravyayasaṃbhavām
english: Dappled with hair for its waterweed, it brought faintness upon the timid; it had its rise in the wasting of the bodies of great elephants, of horses, and of warriors.

sanskrit: śoṇitaughamahāvegāṃ drauṇiḥ prāvartayan nadīm yodhārtaravanirghoṣāṃ kṣatajormisamākulām
english: Droṇa's son set flowing this river, whose mighty current was a flood of blood, whose roar was the anguished cry of warriors, and which surged with waves of gore.

sanskrit: prāyād atimahāghoraṃ yamakṣayamahodadhim nihatya rākṣasān bāṇair drauṇir haiḍimbam ārdayat
english: It coursed onward into the most fearful great ocean that is Yama's abode; and having slain the rākṣasas with his arrows, Droṇa's son fell to tormenting the son of Hiḍimbā.

sanskrit: punar apy atisaṃkruddhaḥ savṛkodarapārṣatān sa nārācagaṇaiḥ pārthān drauṇir viddhvā mahābalaḥ
english: Then once more, in towering wrath, the mighty son of Droṇa pierced the sons of Pṛthā together with Vṛkodara and the grandson of Pṛṣata, smiting them with showers of iron shafts.

sanskrit: jaghāna surathaṃ nāma drupadasya sutaṃ vibhuḥ punaḥ śrutaṃjayaṃ nāma surathasyānujaṃ raṇe
english: The lordly warrior slew Drupada's son named Suratha, and then in battle Śrutaṃjaya, the younger brother of Suratha.

sanskrit: balānīkaṃ jayānīkaṃ jayāśvaṃ cābhijaghnivān śrutāhvayaṃ ca rājendra drauṇir ninye yamakṣayam
english: Balānīka, Jayānīka, and Jayāśva he struck down; and Śrutāhvaya too, O king of kings, the son of Droṇa dispatched to Yama's realm.

sanskrit: tribhiś cānyaiḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ supuṅkhai rukmamālinam śatruṃjayaṃ ca balinaṃ śakralokaṃ nināya ha
english: And with three other keen, well-feathered shafts he led the mighty Śatruṃjaya, garlanded in gold, into the world of Indra.

sanskrit: jaghāna sa pṛṣadhraṃ ca candradevaṃ ca māninam kuntibhojasutāṃś cājau daśabhir daśa jaghnivān
english: He slew Pṛṣadhra and the proud Candradeva, and the sons of Kuntibhoja in that battle he killed, ten of them with ten shafts.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā susaṃkruddhaḥ saṃdhāyogram ajihmagam mumocākarṇapūrṇena dhanuṣā śaram uttamam yamadaṇḍopamaṃ ghoram uddiśyāśu ghaṭotkacam
english: Then Aśvatthāman, in mighty wrath, fitting a dreadful straight-flying shaft, drew the bow to his ear and loosed that surpassing arrow, terrible as the rod of Yama, swiftly aimed at Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: sa bhittvā hṛdayaṃ tasya rākṣasasya mahāśaraḥ viveśa vasudhāṃ śīghraṃ sapuṅkhaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: That great arrow, cleaving the heart of the rākṣasa, swiftly entered the earth, feathers and all, O lord of the world.

sanskrit: taṃ hataṃ patitaṃ jñātvā dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ drauṇeḥ sakāśād rājendra apaninye rathāntaram
english: Knowing him slain and fallen, the great chariot-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O king of kings, bore him away upon another chariot from the presence of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: tathā parāṅmukharathaṃ sainyaṃ yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ nṛpa parājitya raṇe vīro droṇaputro nanāda ha pūjitaḥ sarvabhūtaiś ca tava putraiś ca bhārata
english: And so, O king, having routed in battle the army of Yudhiṣṭhira until its chariots turned their backs, the heroic son of Droṇa roared aloud, honored by all beings and by your sons, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: atha śaraśatabhinnakṛttadehair; hatapatitaiḥ kṣaṇadācaraiḥ samantāt nidhanam upagatair mahī kṛtābhūd; giriśikharair iva durgamātiraudrā
english: Then with the night-rangers slain and fallen on every side, their bodies riven and hacked by hundreds of arrows, the earth was made impassable and most terrible, as though heaped with mountain peaks of the dead.

sanskrit: taṃ siddhagandharvapiśācasaṃghā; nāgāḥ suparṇāḥ pitaro vayāṃsi rakṣogaṇā bhūtagaṇāś ca drauṇim; apūjayann apsarasaḥ surāś ca
english: The hosts of siddhas, gandharvas, and piśācas, the nāgas, the suparṇas, the ancestors, and the birds, the throngs of rākṣasas and the multitudes of spirits, the apsarases and the gods—all honored that son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca drupadasyātmajān dṛṣṭvā kuntibhojasutāṃs tathā droṇaputreṇa nihatān rākṣasāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the sons of Drupada and the sons of Kuntibhoja, and rākṣasas by the thousand, slain by the son of Droṇa—

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro bhīmaseno dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ yuyudhānaś ca saṃyattā yuddhāyaiva mano dadhuḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīmasena, Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata, and Yuyudhāna, girding themselves, set their minds firmly upon battle.

sanskrit: somadattaḥ punaḥ kurddho dṛṣṭvā sātyakim āhave mahatā śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Somadatta, enraged once more at the sight of Sātyaki in the fray, covered him on every side with a mighty rain of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddham atīva bhayavardhanam tvadīyānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca ghoraṃ vijayakāṅkṣiṇām
english: Then there arose a battle exceedingly dreadful and terror-breeding, between your men and the foe, all of them hungering for victory.

sanskrit: daśabhiḥ sātvatasyārthe bhīmo vivyādha kauravam somadatto 'pi taṃ vīraṃ śatena pratyavidhyata
english: For the sake of the Sātvata, Bhīma pierced the Kaurava with ten shafts; and Somadatta in turn struck that hero with a hundred.

sanskrit: sātvatas tv abhisaṃkruddhaḥ putrādhibhir abhiplutam vṛddham ṛddhaṃ guṇaiḥ sarvair yayātim iva nāhuṣam
english: But the Sātvata, mightily enraged, pierced him—aged, yet rich in every virtue like Yayāti the son of Nahuṣa, and overwhelmed with grief for his sons—

sanskrit: vivyādha daśabhis tīkṣṇaiḥ śarair vajranipātibhiḥ śaktyā cainam athāhatya punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: —he pierced him with ten keen shafts that fell like thunderbolts, and striking him with a spear besides, pierced him again with seven.

sanskrit: tatas tu sātyaker arthe bhīmaseno navaṃ dṛḍham mumoca parighaṃ ghoraṃ somadattasya mūrdhani
english: Then, for the sake of Sātyaki, Bhīmasena hurled at the head of Somadatta a fresh and sturdy iron-bound mace, terrible to behold.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cāgnisaṃkāśaṃ mumoca śaram uttamam somadattorasi kruddhaḥ supatraṃ niśitaṃ yudhi
english: And Sātyaki in his wrath loosed at Somadatta's breast a surpassing shaft, fair-feathered and whetted, blazing like fire in the fight.

sanskrit: yugapat petatur atha ghorau parighamārgaṇau śarīre somadattasya sa papāta mahārathaḥ
english: At one and the same moment the dread mace and the arrow fell upon the body of Somadatta, and that great chariot-warrior dropped down.

sanskrit: vyāmohite tu tanaye bāhlīkaḥ samupādravat visṛjañ śaravarṣāṇi kālavarṣīva toyadaḥ
english: When his son was struck senseless, Bāhlika rushed forward, pouring down floods of arrows like a cloud raining at the appointed season.

sanskrit: bhīmo 'tha sātvatasyārthe bāhlīkaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ pīḍayan vai mahātmānaṃ vivyādha raṇamūrdhani
english: Then Bhīma, for the sake of the Sātvata, sorely pressing the great-souled Bāhlika with nine shafts, pierced him at the forefront of the battle.

sanskrit: prātipīyas tu saṃkruddhaḥ śaktiṃ bhīmasya vakṣasi nicakhāna mahābāhuḥ puraṃdara ivāśanim
english: But the son of Pratīpa, enraged, that mighty-armed one, drove a spear into Bhīma's breast as Purandara hurls the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa tayābhihato bhīmaś cakampe ca mumoha ca prāpya cetaś ca balavān gadām asmai sasarja ha
english: Struck by it, Bhīma trembled and swooned; but regaining his senses, the strong one hurled his mace at him.

sanskrit: sā pāṇḍavena prahitā bāhlīkasya śiro 'harat sa papāta hataḥ pṛthvyāṃ vajrāhata ivādrirāṭ
english: Sped by the Pāṇḍava, it carried off Bāhlika's head; and slain, he fell to the earth like a great mountain shattered by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate vīre bāhlīke puruṣarṣabhe putrās te 'bhyardayan bhīmaṃ daśa dāśaratheḥ samāḥ
english: When that hero Bāhlika, that bull among men, was slain, ten of your sons, the equals of the son of Daśaratha, assailed Bhīma.

sanskrit: nārācair daśabhir bhīmas tān nihatya tavātmajān karṇasya dayitaṃ putraṃ vṛṣasenam avākirat
english: Slaying those sons of yours with ten iron shafts, Bhīma then overwhelmed Vṛṣasena, the beloved son of Karṇa.

sanskrit: tato vṛṣaratho nāma bhrātā karṇasya viśrutaḥ jaghāna bhīmaṃ nārācais tam apy abhyavadhīd balī
english: Then Vṛṣaratha, a renowned brother of Karṇa, struck Bhīma with iron shafts; and him too the mighty one slew.

sanskrit: tataḥ sapta rathān vīraḥ syālānāṃ tava bhārata nihatya bhīmo nārācaiḥ śatacandram apothayat
english: Then the hero Bhīma, having slain with his iron shafts seven chariot-warriors among your brothers-in-law, O Bhārata, crushed Śatacandra.

sanskrit: amarṣayanto nihataṃ śatacandraṃ mahāratham śakuner bhrātaro vīrā gajākṣaḥ śarabho vibhuḥ abhidrutya śarais tīkṣṇair bhīmasenam atāḍayan
english: Unable to brook the slaying of the great chariot-warrior Śatacandra, the heroic brothers of Śakuni—Gajākṣa, Śarabha, and Vibhu—rushed upon Bhīmasena and smote him with keen shafts.

sanskrit: sa tudyamāno nārācair vṛṣṭivegair ivarṣabhaḥ jaghāna pañcabhir bāṇaiḥ pañcaivātibalo rathān tān dṛṣṭvā nihatān vīrān vicelur nṛpasattamāḥ
english: Galled by their iron shafts, like a bull beneath the rushing rain, the exceedingly strong Bhīma slew those five chariot-warriors with five arrows; and seeing those heroes slain, the foremost of kings wavered.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kruddhas tavānīkam aśātayat miṣataḥ kumbhayoneś ca putrāṇāṃ ca tavānagha
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira in his wrath shattered your host, before the very eyes of the pitcher-born Droṇa and of your sons, O sinless one.

sanskrit: ambaṣṭhān mālavāñ śūrāṃs trigartān saśibīn api prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya gaṇān yuddhe yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The Ambaṣṭhas, the Mālavas, the valiant Trigartas, and the Śibis as well—these troops Yudhiṣṭhira sent off in battle to the world of Death.

sanskrit: abhīṣāhāñ śūrasenān bāhlīkān savasātikān nikṛtya pṛthivīṃ rājā cakre śoṇitakardamām
english: Cutting down the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Bāhlīkas, and the Vasātis, the king made the earth a mire of blood.

sanskrit: yaudheyāraṭṭarājanyamadrakāṇāṃ gaṇān yudhi prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya śūrān bāṇair yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The valiant troops of the Yaudheyas, the Āraṭṭas, the Rājanyas, and the Madrakas—these Yudhiṣṭhira sent off in battle with his arrows to the world of Death.

sanskrit: hatāharata gṛhṇīta vidhyata vyavakṛntata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdo yudhiṣṭhirarathaṃ prati
english: "Strike! Seize him! Take him! Pierce him! Cut him down!"—such was the tumultuous clamor that rose about the chariot of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sainyāni drāvayantaṃ taṃ droṇo dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiram coditas tava putreṇa sāyakair abhyavākirat
english: Seeing Yudhiṣṭhira routing the troops, Droṇa, urged on by your son, overwhelmed him with arrows.

sanskrit: droṇas tu paramakruddho vāyavyāstreṇa pārthivam vivyādha so 'sya tad divyam astram astreṇa jaghnivān
english: Droṇa, in supreme wrath, pierced the king with the missile of Vāyu; but the other foiled that celestial weapon with a weapon of his own.

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate cāstre bhāradvājo yudhiṣṭhire vāruṇaṃ yāmyam āgneyaṃ tvāṣṭraṃ sāvitram eva ca cikṣepa paramakruddho jighāṃsuḥ pāṇḍunandanam
english: That weapon foiled, the son of Bharadvāja, in supreme wrath and bent on slaying the son of Pāṇḍu, hurled at Yudhiṣṭhira the missiles of Varuṇa, of Yama, of Agni, of Tvaṣṭṛ, and of Savitṛ.

sanskrit: kṣiptāni kṣipyamāṇāni tāni cāstrāṇi dharmajaḥ jaghānāstrair mahābāhuḥ kumbhayoner avitrasan
english: Those weapons, hurled and being hurled, the mighty-armed son of Dharma, unshaken before the pitcher-born one, struck down with weapons of his own.

sanskrit: satyāṃ cikīrṣamāṇas tu pratijñāṃ kumbhasaṃbhavaḥ prāduścakre 'stram aindraṃ vai prājāpatyaṃ ca bhārata jighāṃsur dharmatanayaṃ tava putrahite rataḥ
english: But wishing to make good his vow, the pitcher-born one, intent upon your sons' welfare and bent on slaying the son of Dharma, brought forth the weapon of Indra and that of Prajāpati, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: patiḥ kurūṇāṃ gajasiṃhagāmī; viśālavakṣāḥ pṛthulohitākṣaḥ prāduścakārāstram ahīnatejā; māhendram anyat sa jaghāna te 'stre
english: The lord of the Kurus, moving with the gait of elephant and lion, broad of chest, large and red of eye, undiminished in splendor, brought forth another weapon, the missile of great Indra, and therewith destroyed those two weapons of his.

sanskrit: vihanyamāneṣv astreṣu droṇaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ yudhiṣṭhiravadhaprepsur brāhmam astram udairayat
english: His weapons being thwarted, Droṇa, filled with wrath and longing to slay Yudhiṣṭhira, raised up the weapon of Brahmā.

sanskrit: tato nājñāsiṣaṃ kiṃ cid ghoreṇa tamasāvṛte sarvabhūtāni ca paraṃ trāsaṃ jagmur mahīpate
english: Then I could perceive nothing at all, for a dreadful darkness shrouded everything, and all beings were seized with utmost terror, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: brahmāstram udyataṃ dṛṣṭvā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ brahmāstreṇaiva rājendra tad astraṃ pratyavārayat
english: Seeing the weapon of Brahmā raised aloft, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī warded off that weapon with the weapon of Brahmā itself, O king of kings.

sanskrit: tataḥ sainikamukhyās te praśaśaṃsur nararṣabhau droṇapārthau maheṣvāsau sarvayuddhaviśāradau
english: Then the chief warriors praised those two bulls among men, Droṇa and the son of Pṛthā, great archers both, skilled in every mode of warfare.

sanskrit: tataḥ pramucya kaunteyaṃ droṇo drupadavāhinīm vyadhamad roṣatāmrākṣo vāyavyāstreṇa bhārata
english: Then, leaving aside the son of Kuntī, Droṇa, his eyes red with rage, scattered Drupada's host with the missile of Vāyu, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: te hanyamānā droṇena pāñcālāḥ prādravan bhayāt paśyato bhīmasenasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Smitten by Droṇa, the Pāñcālas fled in terror, before the very eyes of Bhīmasena and the great-souled son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī bhīmaś ca sahasā saṃnyavartatām mahadbhyāṃ rathavaṃśābhyāṃ parigṛhya balaṃ tava
english: Then the Diademed one and Bhīma swiftly turned back, hemming in your army with two great lines of chariots.

sanskrit: bībhatsur dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvam uttaraṃ tu vṛkodaraḥ bhāradvājaṃ śaraughābhyāṃ mahadbhyām abhyavarṣatām
english: Bībhatsu on the right flank, and Vṛkodara on the left, rained down upon the son of Bharadvāja with two mighty floods of arrows.

sanskrit: tau tadā sṛñjayāś caiva pāñcālāś ca mahaujasaḥ anvagacchan mahārāja matsyāś ca saha sātvataiḥ
english: Then the Sṛñjayas and the mighty Pāñcālas followed those two, O great king, and the Matsyas together with the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā bhāratī senā vadhyamānā kirīṭinā droṇena vāryamāṇās te svayaṃ tava sutena ca nāśakyanta mahārāja yodhā vārayituṃ tadā
english: Then that Bhārata army, being slaughtered by the Diademed one, could not be held back—though Droṇa himself and your son strove to restrain them, the warriors could not then be checked, O great king.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca udīryamāṇaṃ tad dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam aviṣahyaṃ ca manvānaḥ karṇaṃ duryodhano 'bravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing that mighty host of the Pāṇḍavas surging up, and deeming it irresistible, Duryodhana spoke to Karṇa.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāpto mitrāṇāṃ mitravatsala trāyasva samare karṇa sarvān yodhān mahābala
english: "The hour has come, O lover of your friends, the hour of friends; save in battle all our warriors, O mighty Karṇa,

sanskrit: pāñcālair matsyakaikeyaiḥ pāṇḍavaiś ca mahārathaiḥ vṛtān samantāt saṃkruddhair niḥśvasadbhir ivoragaiḥ
english: —beset on every side by the Pāñcālas, the Matsyas, the Kaikeyas, and the great chariot-warriors among the Pāṇḍavas, all enraged and hissing like serpents.

sanskrit: ete nadanti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavā jitakāśinaḥ śakropamāś ca bahavaḥ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajāḥ
english: These Pāṇḍavas roar in their exultation, flushed with the look of victory, and many a host of Pāñcāla chariots besides, each rival to Indra."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca paritrātum iha prāpto yadi pārthaṃ puraṃdaraḥ tam apy āśu parājitya tato hantāsmi pāṇḍavam
english: Karṇa said: "Even if Purandara himself should come hither to rescue the son of Pṛthā, swiftly vanquishing him too, I shall thereafter slay the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: satyaṃ te pratijānāmi samāśvasihi bhārata hantāsmi pāṇḍutanayān pāñcālāṃś ca samāgatān
english: Truly I promise you—take heart, O Bhārata—I shall slay the sons of Pāṇḍu and the Pāñcālas gathered against us.

sanskrit: jayaṃ te pratijānāmi vāsavasyeva pāvakiḥ priyaṃ tava mayā kāryam iti jīvāmi pārthiva
english: I promise you victory, as the son of Agni promised it to Vāsava; for I live, O king, only that your good may be wrought by me.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva pārthānāṃ phalguno balavattaraḥ tasyāmoghāṃ vimokṣyāmi śaktiṃ śakravinirmitām
english: Of all the sons of Pṛthā, Phalguna is the strongest; against him I shall loose the unfailing spear fashioned by Śakra.

sanskrit: tasmin hate maheṣvāse bhrātaras tasya mānada tava vaśyā bhaviṣyanti vanaṃ yāsyanti vā punaḥ
english: When that great archer is slain, his brothers, O giver of honor, will fall under your sway, or else go once more to the forest."

sanskrit: mayi jīvati kauravya viṣādaṃ mā kṛthāḥ kva cit ahaṃ jeṣyāmi samare sahitān sarvapāṇḍavān
english: "While I live, O Kaurava, nowhere give way to despair; I shall conquer in battle all the Pāṇḍavas together,

sanskrit: pāñcālān kekayāṃś caiva vṛṣṇīṃś cāpi samāgatān bāṇaughaiḥ śakalīkṛtya tava dāsyāmi medinīm
english: —and the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, and the Vṛṣṇis assembled too; shattering them to fragments with floods of arrows, I shall give you the earth."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ karṇaṃ tu kṛpaḥ śāradvato 'bravīt smayann iva mahābāhuḥ sūtaputram idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: To Karṇa, speaking thus, the mighty-armed Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, replied, smiling as it were, in these words to the charioteer's son:

sanskrit: śobhanaṃ śobhanaṃ karṇa sanāthaḥ kurupuṃgavaḥ tvayā nāthena rādheya vacasā yadi sidhyati
english: "Fine, fine, Karṇa! With you for protector, the bull of the Kurus has indeed found a protector—O Rādheya, if only it could be accomplished by words!

sanskrit: bahuśaḥ katthase karṇa kauravyasya samīpataḥ na tu te vikramaḥ kaś cid dṛśyate balam eva vā
english: Many a time, Karṇa, you boast in the presence of the Kaurava; yet no prowess of yours is anywhere to be seen, nor any strength.

sanskrit: samāgamaḥ pāṇḍusutair dṛṣṭas te bahuśo yudhi sarvatra nirjitaś cāsi pāṇḍavaiḥ sūtanandana
english: Your encounters with the sons of Pāṇḍu have been seen many times in battle, and everywhere you have been vanquished by the Pāṇḍavas, O son of a charioteer.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇe tadā karṇa gandharvair dhṛtarāṣṭraje tadāyudhyanta sainyāni tvam ekas tu palāyathāḥ
english: When the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra was being carried off by the gandharvas, Karṇa, the armies fought on, but you alone took to flight.

sanskrit: virāṭanagare cāpi sametāḥ sarvakauravāḥ pārthena nirjitā yuddhe tvaṃ ca karṇa sahānujaḥ
english: And in the city of Virāṭa too, all the Kauravas gathered together were vanquished in battle by the son of Pṛthā—you as well, Karṇa, together with your brothers.

sanskrit: ekasyāpy asamarthas tvaṃ phalgunasya raṇājire katham utsahase jetuṃ sakṛṣṇān sarvapāṇḍavān
english: Unequal as you are even to Phalguna alone on the field of battle, how do you presume to conquer all the Pāṇḍavas together with Kṛṣṇa?

sanskrit: abruvan karṇa yudhyasva bahu katthasi sūtaja anuktvā vikramed yas tu tad vai satpuruṣavratam
english: Fight without speaking, Karṇa; you boast overmuch, son of a charioteer. To show valor rather than proclaim it—that is the vow of the good.

sanskrit: garjitvā sūtaputra tvaṃ śāradābhram ivājalam niṣphalo dṛśyase karṇa tac ca rājā na budhyate
english: Having thundered like an autumn cloud that holds no water, you are seen, Karṇa, to come to nothing, O son of a charioteer—and this the king does not perceive.

sanskrit: tāvad garjasi rādheya yāvat pārthaṃ na paśyasi purā pārthaṃ hi te dṛṣṭvā durlabhaṃ garjitaṃ bhavet
english: You thunder, Rādheya, only so long as you do not behold the son of Pṛthā; once you have seen him before you, that thundering of yours will be hard to come by."
